name: Cement casing
summary: After a drilling rig runs a string of steel casing into a new well, a cementing crew pumps cement down the casing and up the gap between the casing and the rock, so the well is sealed from groundwater and other zones. A cementing supervisor and two pump operators confirm the well data and the cement program, drive the cementing unit to the lease, wait for the rig to finish running and circulating casing, hold a hazard assessment, rig up and pressure test, then mix and pump spacer and slurry, drop the plug and displace it, and watch for cement returns at surface. The job has to start when the casing lands, at any hour and in any weather, so crews spend much of their time travelling and waiting; equipment failures, float failures and missing cement returns lead to extra work and, for the producer, to a remedial program under AER Directive 009.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company running about 16 cementing units from Alberta and northeast BC district bases with bulk blending plants, plus a Calgary cement and fluids laboratory and engineering office.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB cementing service lines in 2019-2022: dispatch board and phone, ERP inventory, tablet field tickets, lab database and spreadsheets, cement placement software; no automated blending recipe download or live job data streaming to the office as standard.

unit_of_work: one cement job (one casing string on one well)
trigger: Dispatch receives the rig's call that casing is about to be run and issues a dispatch order with the cement program to a cementing crew.
end_state: The casing is cemented, the crew has rigged out and returned to base, and the job report and signed field ticket are submitted; or the job was cancelled before the crew left.

volume.seasonality: Follows the WCSB rig count: highest in January to mid-March, lowest during spring break-up in April and May.

evidence.note: Kept the organisation file's 400 jobs a month; cementing activity tracks the rig count and about 16 units operated (src3). About 25 jobs per unit a month is consistent with surface and production casing on most wells.

surge.cause: Winter drilling and completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Cementing activity tracks the rig count (src3), which peaks in the first quarter; duration and multiplier follow the organisation file's estimate.

About 7.5 hands-on hours a job over 400 jobs (about 23 FTE at 130 productive hours); supervisors on rotation also cover remedial jobs, training and standby, so most of the 40 are stated here; estimate.
Two operators a job for about 12 elapsed hours of travel, rig-up, pumping and rig-out (about 74 FTE at 130 productive hours; field rotations give more paid hours); estimate.
Call-out confirmation and crew assignment, about 20 minutes a job; dispatcher is an organisation file role not listed for this process; estimate.
Program revisions when the well data change, about one job in six; not listed for this process in the organisation file; estimate.

systems.name: Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Electronic field ticketing on tablets, linked to the ERP price book
HSE incident, hazard assessment and audit system
Laboratory test records (lab database and spreadsheets)
Fracture and cement placement modelling software
Vehicle telematics and electronic driver logs
Maintenance work order and equipment history module

steps.name: Confirm call-out and assign crew
steps.description: The dispatcher takes the rig's call with the expected casing landing time, checks which cementing crew and unit are free and within hours, assigns them on the dispatch board and phones the supervisor with the lease location and the job number.

error.defect_description: Wrong lease directions or rig contact passed to the crew

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review cement program and calculate job
steps.description: The cementing supervisor opens the cement program and lab report, checks casing size and depth, hole size, slurry volumes, densities and displacement volume, and works out the pump schedule, expected pressures and the materials and water needed.

evidence.note: Cement programs set coverage, volumes and placement (src2); times are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm well data with the customer
steps.description: The supervisor phones the customer's wellsite supervisor to confirm the casing tally and shoe depth, float equipment, final hole size or caliper, mud weight and the required cement top, and notes any change from the program.

next.condition: depth, hole size or cement top changed

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Revise program for changed well data
steps.description: The cement engineer reruns volumes and placement for the new depth, caliper or cement top, checks the slurry's thickening time still covers the longer job, and emails a revised program to the supervisor and bulk plant.

error.defect_description: Bulk plant not told of extra tonnage

evidence.note: Required cement tops and caliper-based volumes with at least 20% excess (Directive 009 items 9-10, src1); frequency and times are estimates.

steps.name: Inspect and load the cementing unit
steps.description: The two operators complete the pre-trip inspection of the cementing unit, check the treating iron certificates, load spacer and wash chemicals, plugs and the cement head, and fill water tanks if the lease has no water.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for call-out time
steps.description: The crew waits at the base or in town until the rig is close to landing casing; rigs move the time when drilling or casing runs go faster or slower, and occasionally cancel or postpone the job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Drive cementing unit to the lease
steps.description: The operators drive the cementing unit and any pickup with chemicals to the lease, usually two to four hours on highway and lease roads, slowed by snow, ice and spring road bans.

evidence.note: Road bans reduce allowed weights during thaw (src9); distances and times are estimates.

steps.name: Drive supervisor pickup to the lease
steps.description: The supervisor drives separately in a crew pickup, calling the rig on the way for an updated casing depth and rig status, and arrives with the job paperwork and data acquisition laptop.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for the rig to land and circulate casing
steps.description: The crew waits on location while the rig finishes running casing, lands it and circulates the hole clean; waits range from minutes to most of a shift when casing runs are slow or the hole is tight.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Hold hazard assessment and pre-job safety meeting
steps.description: The supervisor checks in with the customer's wellsite supervisor and the rig manager, completes the field level hazard assessment for the job with the crew, and leads the pre-job safety meeting with rig and service hands on pressure areas, muster points and roles.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 sections 7-8: hazard assessment before work begins, with worker participation; customer site safety rules

evidence.note: OHS Code Part 2 hazard assessment and worker participation (src8); times are estimates.

steps.name: Rig up to the casing
steps.description: The operators spot the unit, lay treating iron from the unit to the cement head on the casing, connect water and bulk supply lines, load the plugs into the cement head and set up density and pressure sensors.

error.defect_description: Hammer union or seal not made up fully

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Pressure test the lines
steps.description: The operators fill the lines and raise pressure in steps to a test pressure above the highest expected job pressure, hold it and watch for leaks while everyone stays out of the line-of-fire area.

control.basis: Company pressure pumping standard: pressure test of treating lines above maximum expected pressure before pumping

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Agree final job plan with the customer
steps.description: The supervisor goes over final slurry and displacement volumes, excess, pump rates and pressure limits with the customer's wellsite supervisor, confirms the rig has finished circulating, and gets the go-ahead to pump.

control.basis: AER Directive 009 items 4 and 10: surface casing cemented full length; production and intermediate volumes from caliper log plus at least 20% excess (licensee's requirement, applied through the program)

evidence.note: Full-length surface cementing and 20% excess requirements (src1); times are estimates.

steps.name: Pump spacer and mix slurry
steps.description: The operators pump the spacer, then mix the lead and tail slurries on the fly from the bulk supply and water, holding density to the program while pumping at the planned rate.

error.defect_description: Slurry density drifts out of range for part of the job

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Monitor density, pressure and returns
steps.description: The supervisor watches density, rate and pressure on the acquisition screen, checks mud returns at the shaker with the rig crew, logs volumes pumped and calls corrections to the operators.

control.basis: AER Directive 009 items 15-16: flow returns visually monitored during cementing and full details of the operation recorded

next.condition: pump, mixer or bulk supply fails

evidence.note: Return monitoring and recording requirements (src1); failure share is an estimate.

steps.name: Manage equipment failure during the job
steps.description: The supervisor decides whether to finish on the backup pump, slow the rate or stop, keeps the slurry moving if possible, tells the customer and calls the district for repair or a backup unit, then records the event for an incident and repair report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Drop plug and displace
steps.description: The operators release the top plug and pump displacement fluid at the planned volume, slow down near the end, bump the plug at the calculated volume and bleed back to check the float equipment holds.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Shut in for failed floats
steps.description: When the floats leak back, the supervisor agrees with the customer to shut in the casing with pressure held until the cement sets, and the crew keeps the unit rigged up and watches the pressure.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check cement returns and record the job
steps.description: The supervisor records whether cement came back to surface, the volume of returns and any losses, compares them with the program, and notes the result for the customer's casing cement report.

control.basis: AER Directive 009 items 5, 15 and 16: cement top determined and AER contacted if surface casing returns are not obtained; cement-top log and remedial program for production casing

evidence.note: Requirements when returns are missing (src1); share of jobs without full returns is an estimate.

steps.name: Report missing returns to the customer
steps.description: The supervisor tells the customer's wellsite supervisor that returns were lost or short, records the estimated cement top and losses, and passes a remedial request (top-up or squeeze) to the district so the producer can meet its Directive 009 duty.

evidence.note: Licensee must determine the cement top and contact the AER (src1); the service company's role is an estimate.

steps.name: Wash up and rig out
steps.description: The operators flush the unit and lines with water, break down and load the treating iron, clean up any spilled cement and leave the cement head for the rig or load it back on the unit.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Complete job report and field ticket
steps.description: While the crew rigs out, the supervisor completes the job report and electronic field ticket: materials and volumes pumped, unit and crew hours, pressures, returns and any extra charges.

error.defect_description: Missing materials or hours on the ticket

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Customer signs field ticket
steps.description: The customer's wellsite supervisor reviews the ticket items and job report on the tablet and signs, or asks for a change to charges, volumes or hours.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Drive back to base
steps.description: The operators drive the unit back to the district base, fuel it and park it, and the supervisor follows in the pickup; long drives at the end of a shift are a fatigue risk managed by journey management.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Debrief and hand in job records
steps.description: The supervisor submits the job report and data file, reports equipment defects in the maintenance system and any incident in the HSE system, and briefs the district on anything the next job needs to know.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Well data changed
exceptions.description: Depth, hole size or required cement top differ from the program, so the engineer revises volumes before the job.

exceptions.name: Job cancelled or postponed
exceptions.description: The rig cancels or postpones the job before the crew leaves.

exceptions.name: Leak on pressure test
exceptions.description: A connection leaks and must be remade before pumping.

exceptions.name: Equipment failure during the job
exceptions.description: A pump, mixer or bulk supply problem forces a backup pump or a slower rate; it creates repair and incident reports and can lead to remedial work.

exceptions.name: Floats do not hold
exceptions.description: Casing is shut in with pressure held until the cement sets.

exceptions.name: No or low cement returns
exceptions.description: Cement did not reach surface or returns were short; a remedial request goes to the district and the producer deals with the AER.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from dispatch order to job records handed in

evidence.note: Estimate: dispatch orders usually reach the crew the day before the job; crews then spend 10 to 18 hours on preparation, travel, waiting and pumping, and hand in records at the end of the shift or the next morning.

benchmarks.unit: kPa after 48 hours at the temperature of the uppermost hydrocarbon zone
benchmarks.population: Production and intermediate casing slurries with fillers, Alberta

evidence.note: Directive 009 item 11 (src1).
Annual average cementing units in the field (src3).

pain_points.description: Crews and units wait for the rig to call them out and again on location while casing is run and circulated; this ties up units that are already fully booked in winter.

evidence.note: Cementing follows the rig count and unit numbers are fixed (src3); waiting times are estimates.

pain_points.description: Well data change at the last minute (deeper casing point, larger hole), forcing program revisions and extra blend.

evidence.note: Typical practice: the final caliper and casing tally are only known shortly before the job.

pain_points.description: Lost or short returns lead to cement-top logs and remedial work for the producer and can damage the relationship with the customer.

evidence.note: Remedial requirements when returns are not obtained (src1).

pain_points.description: Long drives before and after long shifts expose crews to fatigue and winter road risk.

evidence.note: Typical practice; journey management is common in the WCSB.

sources.title: Directive 009: Casing Cementing Minimum Requirements (edition of May 14, 2025)
sources.supports: Licensee is responsible for satisfactory cementing. Surface casing cemented full length; if returns are not obtained or the annular level drops, the cement top must be determined and the AER contacted about remedial action (items 4-5). Surface casing centralized top, bottom and every 50 m (item 7). Production and intermediate cement volume from caliper log plus at least 20% excess (item 10). Fillers allowed only if compressive strength is at least 3,500 kPa after 48 hours at the temperature of the uppermost hydrocarbon zone, using 4.4 C surface and 2.7 C/100 m where unknown (items 11-12). Flow returns visually monitored during cementing; cement-top log and remedial program to the AER within 60 days of rig release when returns are missing (item 15). Full details recorded on tour reports or a casing cement report (item 16). Required cement tops by township from figure 1 (items 9, 24). The 2025 edition only adds brine-hosted minerals to the 2022 edition; the same requirements applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Cementing
sources.supports: Cement programs prepared by engineers using simulation software for slurry placement, sheath integrity, wellbore properties and temperature; pre-flushes and spacers; surface, intermediate, production, liner, horizontal, plug, remedial and squeeze cementing; lost-circulation blends for the WCSB; R&D facilities and operational support laboratories with lab technicians.

sources.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Cementing activity tracks the WCSB rig count (201 rigs in Q4 2022, 176 in Q4 2021); 17 cementing units operated in Q4 2022; annual average of 16 cementing units in the field in 2021 and 2022; cementing about 16-19% of revenue; 1,335,000 tonnes of proppant pumped in 2022 and 1,364,000 in 2021; oilfield cement and proppant sourced from suppliers in Canada and the United States.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code (table of contents)
sources.supports: Part 2 Hazard Assessment, Elimination and Control: section 7 hazard assessment, section 8 worker participation, section 9 hazard elimination and control; Part 4 harmful substances including section 28 general provisions for asbestos, silica, coal dust and lead and section 40 health assessments for silica exposure; Part 18 respiratory protective equipment.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans lower maximum weights when roads are weak or thawing; spring heavy-haul period starts when thaw depth reaches 25 cm, post-thaw from about June 16; exemptions by permit through the Central Permit Office; local bans set by counties and municipal districts.

assumptions: Loaded hourly costs and headcounts are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.35).

A crew is one cementing supervisor and two pump operators, as the organisation file's cementing crew resource says; the operators attend the hazard assessment and pre-job meeting, but that time is only counted for the supervisor.

Bulk truck drivers take part in the job but their time and trucks are counted in the bulk blending and delivery process, so the bulk-truck-driver role and bulk truck resource listed in the process_map are left out here.
Directive 009 duties belong to the licensee (the producer); the cementing crew supplies the job record and follows the program.

Unit and crew hours held per job (about 14 to 15 hours including travel and waiting) times 400 jobs a month exceed the organisation file's 16-17 units at a mode of 200 available hours a month; either the available hours or the job volume in the organisation file is low.
Dispatcher and design engineer take part but are not listed among the process_map roles.

The simulated median cycle time (about 2 days) is slightly above the benchmark estimate of 1.7 days because the triangular waits for the call-out and on location have long upper tails; both rest on estimates, not measured job logs.
